question: (A) With the board's minimums as hard floors (Q18.2-Q18.5: track width, via diameter, via drill and annular ring, copper-to-edge and copper-to-hole clearance), does enhanced ship zero routing-caused KiCad track_width, via_diameter, annular_width, drill_out_of_range, copper_edge_clearance and hole_clearance errors on the five rows whose baseline breaks them, and what does it cost in unconnected items? (B) With the floors in both arms, does strict transactional rip-up (Q11) leave fewer KiCad-unconnected items after pass 1 than Java's rip-up on Q11's eligible rows, with no hard breach, no board worse than twice its band and drc_real not worse?
rule_text: pair (before, mp1) is the floors' cost: the floors are a decided correctness rule (decided 2026-10-20: routing never breaks the board's minimum manufacturing rules; correctness wins over completion), so it is judged on its hard metrics only (below_minimum = 0, edge_clearance = 0, hole_clearance = 0 and via_in_pad = 0 in mp1 and strict on every pair-A row); its totals line and every unconnected change are reported, not judged. Pair (mp1, strict) is judged by N02's totals rule (freerouting-dev gate --prereg on its records file, --eligible): hard metrics raw (no baseline subtraction: every arm must have 0), guards drc_real and pour_lost_pins not worse than mp1, no board worse than twice its band, and the summed signal improved by more than the set noise

before.engine: freerouting-rs release CLI of branch land/q18 (main 038e0f5 plus Q18.2-Q18.5), one Linux build of freerouting-cli and freerouting-dev from its worktree for every arm (its --version and sha256 in the done note); the default profile enhanced
before.what: main's behaviour (Q11's mp1 command): no board minimum known and none derived; every Q18 code path then computes what main computes (no floor, no via change), so this arm is main without a second build

mp1.engine: freerouting-rs release CLI of branch land/q18 (main 038e0f5 plus Q18.2-Q18.5), one Linux build of freerouting-cli and freerouting-dev from its worktree for every arm (its --version and sha256 in the done note); the default profile enhanced
mp1.what: the floors: Q11's mp1 command plus the row's Board Setup minimums from tools/bench/sets/q18-board-minimums.txt (ROW_FLAGS=1, the plugin's flags); the fixture rows have none, so enhanced's from_classes floors them at their narrowest class width

strict.engine: freerouting-rs release CLI of branch land/q18 (main 038e0f5 plus Q18.2-Q18.5), one Linux build of freerouting-cli and freerouting-dev from its worktree for every arm (its --version and sha256 in the done note); the default profile enhanced
strict.what: candidate: mp1 with Q11's strict transactional rip-up

pairs_rule: pair A (before, mp1) on the five rows whose baseline grades break the minimums (laser-backplane, mydevboard, slice, vfo: Q11.6's KiCad track_width 10, 74, 16, 72 and copper_edge_clearance mydevboard 18, vfo 4; d3c-0496-kitspace-f-91w: N03's tree+nodes session graded under the board's own rules by Q19's fixed grade.sh (bed86e2, target/orchestrator/q19/out/grade/fixed/), annular_width 59, hole_clearance 40, copper_edge_clearance 40, track_width 36), judged as rule_text says, with strict's hard metrics on the same rows reported next to them; pair B (mp1, strict) on Q11's 11 eligible rows, judged by the totals rule. before runs the five pair-A rows only; mp1 and strict run every row of the set

boards.eligibility: pair B: Q11.json's `eligible` (the 11 rows Q11.6's mp1 left incomplete), fixed here before any run; pair A: the five rows named in pairs_rule
boards.board_flags: the set file's per-row flags (ROW_FLAGS=1): each row's Board Setup minimums from its KiCad project, as the plugin passes them; the arms' common flags are in every command
boards.why: Q11's eligible quick rows: Q18 re-measures Q11.6 with the floors; pair A's rows are the ones whose baseline breaks the minimums (d3c-0496 added for the via and hole floors, decided 2026-10-20)

grading: as Q11.json amendment 2 (2): canary-pwr-9511d9a by Q10's canary grade, the corpus rows (target/corpus and target/corpus-d3c) by tools/kicad-oracle/grade.sh at main 038e0f5 or later (Q19's bed86e2: a board without a .kicad_pro graded under the rules KiCad migrates from it, summary `rules`) through tools/bench/grade-distinct.sh (one KiCad grade per distinct session), the benchmark rows not graded; kicad-cli only while `pgrep -a kicad-cli` shows none

metric_definitions.below_minimum: raw, not relative to a baseline (decided 2026-10-20: 'no new breach versus baseline' no longer applies to the board minimums). Graded rows: KiCad's routing-caused (drc_real_by_type, routed minus input) track_width + via_diameter + annular_width + drill_out_of_range errors (canary: the same error types of its grade); benchmark rows: the session's traces narrower than the board's narrowest class width that the input does not have (Q11.json amendment 2's scratch tool q11m, at this build)
metric_definitions.edge_clearance: routing-caused copper-to-edge errors, raw: graded rows drc_real_by_type.copper_edge_clearance (KiCad's routed DRC minus the input's, grade.sh); canary error:copper_edge_clearance; benchmark rows null (not graded)
metric_definitions.kicad_unconnected: KiCad's unconnected items after importing the session
metric_definitions.wall_seconds: /usr/bin/time's elapsed seconds; other sessions' routes may overlap: reported, not compared
metric_definitions.hole_clearance: routing-caused copper-to-hole errors, raw: graded rows drc_real_by_type.hole_clearance; canary error:hole_clearance; benchmark rows null (not graded)

extra_reported: the job log's 'Transactional rip-up' tally per strict row
the floors' unconnected cost per pair-A row and summed
solder_mask_bridge per graded row (routing-caused, drc_real_by_type), reported, not judged (Q18's solder-mask item)
keep_rule: pair A: the floors stay (decided), with enhanced's from_classes, if mp1 has no hard breach on the pair-A rows; a breach left is a bug fixed before Q18 closes. Pair B: strict goes to Q18.9 (promotion into enhanced through N05) only if it passes the totals rule against mp1; otherwise it stays a setting off by default (decided 2026-10-20: kept, not removed)
stop_rule: one registered run per arm per row; no reruns with other settings
not_registered: strict against Q11's ripcost-best (dropped: two arms where the question allows)

decision_table.pass: Q18.9: an ENHANCED entry for router.autorouter.connection_router = transactional-ripup with its DIVERGENCES line, settings test and N05.3 entry
decision_table.fail: strict stays a setting off by default and in no profile; the numbers go into Q18.6's note

timing: measured after Q18.2-Q18.5 are in the build; rewritten 2026-10-20 before any run when the via and hole floors joined Q18 (d3c-0496 added, the set cut to the rows an arm runs, hole_clearance a hard metric), and again before any run for Q19's grader fix (d3c-0496's flags from its own rules)

amendments.change: edge_clearance and hole_clearance: role hard -> guard in the gate
amendments.reason: freerouting-dev gate refuses a null hard metric (UNGRADED), and the five fixtures/Issue*.dsn rows have no KiCad project, so KiCad cannot grade their edge or hole clearance (metric_definitions already said null). Their zero requirement on every graded row is unchanged and is checked from the records table (Q18.6's accept clause); the gate judges them as guards (not worse than mp1) where graded. No number changes; no rerun.

amendments.change: d3c-0496-kitspace-f-91w leaves pair A: reported as information, not judged and not a guard (pair_a_rows 5 -> 4, new information_rows); its routes and grades are kept
amendments.reason: decided 2026-10-20: KiCad-graded rows use only boards whose project has its own .kicad_pro (KiCad 6 or later). d3c-0496 is a KiCad 4 board; the rules KiCad invents on conversion contradict the design (its own 0.46/0.3 mm net class via has a 0.08 mm annular ring against the converted 0.1 mm minimum), so a floor there chases a board-data conflict, not a router bug. Its numbers existed when this was decided, so the row is amended, not deleted.
